title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to consume enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. However, many pregnant women struggle to find recipes rich in iron and folate.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two crucial nutrients during pregnancy. Iron can be found in foods like red meat, chicken, fish, and leafy greens like spinach and kale. Folate is abundant in leafy greens like spinach and kale, as well as citrus fruits like oranges and grapefruits. Vitamin C also plays a vital role in enhancing iron absorption.

## Recipes
Here are three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in 30 minutes:

* Grilled chicken and vegetable bowl with brown rice and a slice of orange: This recipe is simple and nutritious. Pregnant women can grill chicken with a bit of olive oil and seasoning, then serve with brown rice, steamed vegetables, and a slice of orange.
* Baked salmon and quinoa bowl with roasted vegetables and a squeeze of lemon: Salmon is an excellent source of iron and folate. Pregnant women can bake salmon with a bit of olive oil and seasoning, then serve with quinoa, roasted vegetables, and a squeeze of lemon.
* Beef and vegetable stir-fry with brown rice and a side of steamed broccoli: Beef is a good source of iron and folate. Pregnant women can stir-fry beef with a bit of olive oil and seasoning, then serve with brown rice, steamed broccoli, and a side of steamed vegetables.

## Food Safety Notes
When cooking for pregnant women, it's essential to consider food safety. According to the CDC, pregnant women should avoid eating foods like sushi, sashimi, and undercooked or raw meat. Additionally, pregnant women should avoid eating foods that contain listeria, such as soft cheeses and cold cuts.

## Practical Tips
To enhance iron absorption, pregnant women can consume vitamin C with their meals. Additionally, pregnant women should drink plenty of water and limit their intake of coffee and tea, as they can reduce iron absorption.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about nutrition or food safety, they should consult their healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. To learn more about iron-and-folate-rich recipes, pregnant women can visit our [meal planner page](/planner) or [read more about prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition).
